content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E22","hypothesis_id":"H04","title":"Operando IR/EPR donor-adduct screen","purpose":"Test whether TEA versus TEOA causes different donor-associated cobalt or substrate-bound species under matched P01 conditions, while bounding what any spectral differences can and cannot establish about the CO/H2 shift.","evidence_ids":["GX011","EV068","EV016","EV085"],"source_to_proposal":"GX011 suggests TEOA can form catalyst adduct-like species in a bipyridine carbonyl system, motivating a cautious transfer test for donor-specific adduct chemistry in Co-bpy rather than assuming the same species. EV016 shows EPR can detect TEOA-derived radicals and that TEA/TEOA can differ in line shape because of physical properties, supporting donor-comparative EPR with matched blanks. EV068 supports operando FTIR/EPR to follow working-state interactions instead of recovered samples only. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and decomposition-derived active species can confound assignments, so donor-free and no-cobalt controls are required and any signal must be treated as descriptive unless tied to matched catalytic outputs.","groups":[{"id":"E22G01","description":"Baseline P01-like reaction mixture with TEOA under CO2 and illumination for near-operando IR/EPR Reproducible donor-specific IR bands or EPR features under otherwise matched conditions would support a cobalt-speciation or donor-adduct contribution, but not by itself prove causality for CO/H2."},{"group_a":"E22G01","group_b":"E22G03","changed_factors":["donor"],"inference":"Tests whether TEOA-dependent features require the donor. Features absent without donor are consistent with donor-derived radicals, donor binding, or donor-enabled substrate intermediates, but remain assignment-limited."},{"group_a":"E22G01","group_b":"E22G04","changed_factors":["cobalt_component"],"inference":"Tests whether candidate features require cobalt. Signals present in both groups are background from donor, support, solvent, or CO2 handling rather than cobalt-specific species."},{"group_a":"E22G01","group_b":"E22G05","changed_factors":["illumination"],"inference":"Tests whether candidate TEOA-associated features are light-generated. A light-only appearance supports turnover-related or photogenerated species; persistence in dark suggests pre-equilibrium binding or background chemistry."}],"procedure":["Prepare matched baseline-family mixtures using the verified P01 component identities; keep vessel geometry, gas handling, solvent ratio, and sampling timing identical across groups.","Run a short pilot to choose concentration and optical path windows that avoid detector saturation and give measurable cobalt-region EPR/IR baselines; lock those settings before the TEA versus TEOA comparison.","Collect dark/background spectra first, then acquire operando or rapid sealed near-operando IR and EPR data under CO2 during illumination for each group using the same time points.","Pair the spectral campaign with matched product analysis from the same batches or parallel identically prepared batches so spectral differences can be compared with CO and H2 outputs without assuming causation.","Use replicate preparations and conservative peak assignment rules, reporting unmatched or ambiguous features as unknown signals rather than named intermediates."],"measurements":["In situ or near-operando IR difference spectra under CO2 and illumination, tracking donor-dependent new bands, band shifts, and growth/decay behavior relative to dark and donor-free baselines.","In situ or rapid-freeze/rapid-transfer EPR spectra, tracking appearance, disappearance, g-pattern changes, and line broadening under TEA versus TEOA conditions.","Matched catalytic readouts from parallel or same-batch experiments: CO and H2 amounts or rates, reported together rather than selectivity alone.","Background spectra from donor-free, no-cobalt, and dark controls to establish which signals are not cobalt-specific or not light-dependent.","If signal strength allows, time ordering of spectral changes relative to product formation; this can show correlation but cannot by itself identify the sole active species."],"supports":"H04 is supported if, under the locked matched P01 comparison, TEA and TEOA show reproducibly different cobalt-requiring and light-dependent IR and/or EPR signatures, or different persistence/loss of such signatures over time, and those differences track a donor-dependent CO/H2 change better than donor-free or no-cobalt backgrounds do.","refutes":"H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-requiring, light-dependent IR/EPR observables within detection limits while catalytic CO/H2 still differs under the same matched conditions, favoring explanations upstream in donor photochemistry or downstream in proton/CO2 handling rather than cobalt-state divergence.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if spectra are too weak, dominated by background/support signals, changed by viscosity or other physical effects without cobalt specificity, or if donor-dependent signals appear but cannot be distinguished from donor decomposition, generic radical formation, or unsupported assignments. Correlation without clean controls also remains inconclusive.","parameter_selection":"Use the literature-backed P01 formulation family only for component identity, not exact invented numbers. First verify the baseline recipe from source records. Then run pilots to set sample concentration, path length, irradiation interval, and EPR acquisition mode by the rule that cobalt-containing samples must show stable unsaturated baselines and donor-free/no-cobalt controls must remain interpretable. If TEA and TEOA differ strongly in viscosity or optical density, adjust only the measurement configuration, not the chemical formulation, and document that this preserves matched chemistry while changing detection settings. Choose time points by a calibration run that captures pre-illumination, early illumination, and a later turnover window without exhausting the sample.","limitations":"Assignments are transferred from nonidentical systems and may not map to Co-bpy. IR/EPR can reveal donor-dependent species or state changes but cannot alone establish the full catalytic mechanism, the exact structure of the active cobalt species, or product origin. TEA/TEOA physical-property differences can alter line shape and transport, so apparent spectral differences are not automatically chemical. Near-operando aliquots may miss the true instantaneous working state. No-cobalt control uses a different total composition and is a background screen, not a full single-factor catalytic comparison.","feasibility":"specialist"}]}
